title: From MCP to Scale: Pipelines That Build Themselves — Rafael Levi, Bright Data
talk_summary: A Bright Data demo showing how to have an agent build a reusable scraper/parser script (via MCP + skills) instead of having the LLM parse raw HTML on every page, then schedule it to self-validate and self-heal. The core transferable idea is 'build a deterministic tool once, then call it cheaply' rather than re-reasoning over large inputs each run.

takeaways.technique: Compile repeated LLM work into a reusable script/tool
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking the LLM to parse HTML every time, the agent writes a parser script once; subsequent runs execute the script and only feed compact JSON back to the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I always ask build a script that can later on be used by it. It's using its own script to save the tokens.
takeaways.numbers: ~62% token save on one site; ~1M tokens saved over 3 pages vs LLM parsing; script run ~60-100 tokens vs ~10,000 for JSON reasoning

takeaways.what_they_do: A pool spins up every 30 minutes, checks whether collected data is valid, fixes breakage, and shuts down if all is fine.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every 30 minutes I have an LLM class pool spools up. It checks what the data is collected... If for this example, there's a always set a validation for data

takeaways.technique: Skills repo the agent pulls from before acting
takeaways.what_they_do: A GitHub 'skills' repo gives the agent best-practice docs and tooling so it builds pipelines correctly without re-deriving approach each time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your agent has everything that it might need... scrape builders back practices, how to everything

takeaways.technique: Cheap model sufficient when task is well-scaffolded
takeaways.what_they_do: For browsing/execution tasks they use a small model because the hard part (anti-bot, tooling) is handled by infrastructure, not the model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: with Claude Haiku model is more than enough for browsing. If it's being masked that it's a real human, it works just fine.

takeaways.technique: Structured JSON over raw/markdown for downstream reasoning
takeaways.what_they_do: Pipeline outputs compact JSON schema so the model reasons over structured fields rather than raw HTML/markdown.
takeaways.evidence_quote: now we're working with a JSON and JSON is much more token efficient than any markdown or any other file
